content.value_statement: Astronomy workflows require reliable handling of coordinates, units, FITS files, time systems, and cosmology. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Astropy patterns for scientific analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains Astropy units and quantity conversions for physics and astronomy calculations.
Guides celestial coordinate creation, frame transformations, angular separation, and catalog matching.
Supports FITS file reading, writing, header inspection, table access, and large-file memory mapping.
Describes Astropy table workflows for filtering, sorting, joining, masking, and unit-aware columns.
Covers precise time formats, time scales, TimeDelta arithmetic, and observing-related time calculations.
Helps with cosmology models, distance calculations, WCS transformations, visualization, and astronomy constants.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not validate the scientific quality of input data.
Astropy and optional dependencies must be installed in the user environment before code can run.
Remote downloads and named-object queries require network access and user-approved data sources.
Large FITS files can still require substantial disk, memory, or processing time.

use_cases.title: Reduce Telescope Observations
use_cases.description: Read FITS files, inspect headers, extract image data, and apply basic array analysis steps.

use_cases.title: Cross-Match Source Catalogs
use_cases.description: Transform coordinates, match sky positions, filter by separation, and prepare joined tables.

use_cases.title: Build Teaching Examples
use_cases.description: Create clear examples for units, time scales, cosmological distances, and WCS transformations.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Units
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Astropy units to convert 12 parsecs into kilometers. Explain why attaching units prevents mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Transform Coordinates
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to create an ICRS coordinate, transform it to Galactic coordinates, and compute separation from another target.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect FITS Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through opening a FITS file, checking HDU structure, reading image data, and reviewing important header values.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Analysis Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an Astropy workflow that reads a catalog, applies units, matches coordinates, computes cosmological distances, and writes results.

output_examples.input: Convert 12 parsecs to kilometers with Astropy units.
output_examples.output: The response explains that the distance should be stored as a quantity, converted to kilometers, and reported with units attached.

output_examples.input: Open a FITS image and summarize useful metadata.
output_examples.output: The response lists the HDU structure, image dimensions, exposure metadata, filter name, and safe next steps for analysis.

output_examples.input: Cross-match two catalogs by sky position.
output_examples.output: The response describes building coordinate objects, matching nearest neighbors, applying an angular threshold, and producing matched table rows.

best_practices: Always attach units to numeric quantities before calculations or conversions.
Use context managers when opening FITS files so file handles close reliably.
State coordinate frames, time scales, cosmology models, and data assumptions explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unitless arrays with physical quantities in the same calculation.
Do not modify FITS structural keywords unless you understand the FITS standard.
Do not download remote astronomy data without user approval and a trusted source.

faq.question: What is Astropy used for?
faq.answer: Astropy is a Python library for astronomy data analysis, including coordinates, units, FITS files, tables, time, cosmology, and WCS.

faq.question: Can this skill write runnable Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide Python examples for Astropy workflows when the user environment has the needed packages installed.

faq.question: Does it support FITS files?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers opening FITS files, inspecting HDUs, reading data, editing headers, writing files, and handling large files.

faq.question: Can it help with coordinate transformations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SkyCoord, common reference frames, observer-dependent frames, angular separation, and catalog matching.

faq.question: Does it fetch data from the internet?
faq.answer: It can explain Astropy download helpers, but network access depends on user approval, environment settings, and trusted data sources.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for scientific review?
faq.answer: No. Users should still verify assumptions, calibrations, data quality, and domain-specific interpretation.
